messages:
sam: Quick follow-up to the authz RFC — we need to decide final semantics for service API keys: should they be treated as independent service principals with explicit role bindings, or as lightweight proxies that inherit their hosting project's RBAC?
lia: Prefer independent principals. Inheritance leaks ownership and makes least-privilege guarantees fragile.
matt: The UX teams worry explicit bindings for every short-lived job is too heavy. They want something like an ephemeral lease that can inherit for N hours.
katie: Could do ephemeral inheritance for dev/test only. Production long-lived keys should be explicit. That gives a path to fast iteration without sacrificing prod controls.
sam: Good compromise. We should also decide schema for bindings. Proposal A: roles array. Proposal B: allow expressions (resource patterns + verbs) for fine-grained rules.
lia: Expressions are powerful but complicate audit and policy eval. Keep roles simple for now and add RBAC->expression mapping later.
matt: For migration: we have ~4k existing service keys with mixed scoping. We need an automated tool to infer minimal explicit bindings and create PRs or owners' approvals.
katie: I'll own the scanner. Plan: collect 30 days of auth logs, map used endpoints to role candidates, propose bindings, and create infra PRs tagged with owners.
infra-bot: Note: current policy DB accepts both "roles": [..] and "scope_expr": ".." fields. No enforcement tiering yet.
sam: Runtime enforcement considerations: deny-by-default, allow-explicit, and block inherited keys from crossing org boundaries. If an inherited ephemeral key is used to call a different project, fail at gateway.
lia: Add requirement: any key marked "inherits" must carry a provenance tag with who enabled it and an expiration timestamp. Also require org-admin signoff for enabling inheritance.
matt: Dev ergonomics: authz-lint CLI that simulates a job using a temp dry-run key and reports minimal roles required. That avoids wide-scoped keys.
katie: Also recommend issuing ephemeral tokens via a token-exchange flow: service key -> short-lived token scoped to roles for runtime. That way we can rotate/kill long-lived keys easily.
sam: Good. Let's define default policy: 1) deny-by-default for service keys, 2) explicit role bindings for production keys, 3) ephemeral inheritance opt-in for dev with 24h max and admin approval, 4) forbid cross-org usage unless allowlisted.
lia: Add audit automation: weekly reports of keys with inheritance enabled, keys with >30d continuous privileged use, and keys without recent owner contact.
matt: For the scanner output format, CSV + JSON PR: include key_id, inferred_roles[], last_seen_ts, suggested_expiry, owner_hint.
katie: I'll wire the scanner into CI so infra PRs block merges until owner ack. Also add a job to rotate/expire flagged keys.
infra-bot: Created infra tickets AUTH-7102 (scanner) and POLICY-332 (inheritance opt-in UX).
sam: Action items: katie build scanner + CI gating, matt prototype authz-lint dry-run, lia draft admin approval flow and audit reports, infra add runtime block for cross-org.
lia: One more edge: service-to-service impersonation. We should disallow service keys from impersonating human users unless explicitly annotated and reviewed.
matt: Agreed, add explicit "impersonation_allowed": false default.
sam: Consensus: explicit-by-default with tightly-scoped opt-in ephemeral inheritance for non-prod, automated scanner/migration plus audit and CI gates. We'll fold this into the next auth rollout timeline. Thanks! :shipit:
